title: Heavy metals in coffee: stop panicking, start asking for COAs
paper: FDA/EFSA contaminant guidance + coffee supply-chain testing practice
finding: The useful clean-coffee question is not whether scary elements exist in the universe. It is whether the brand can show current batch testing for lead, cadmium, arsenic, and mercury, plus origin and roast-date transparency.

title: Mold-free coffee claims need lab receipts, not wellness theater
paper: Coffee mycotoxin literature + buyer transparency audit
finding: Ochratoxin A and aflatoxin testing are legitimate signals. A mold-free badge with no lab, batch, date, analytes, or numeric result is just a sticker doing cardio.

title: Decaf purity starts with process disclosure
paper: Decaffeination process and residue standards context
finding: Swiss Water and CO₂ decaf are clean default signals because the process is clear. Mystery decaf is not automatically dangerous, but the lack of disclosure is a buyer red flag.

title: The nine-question clean-coffee buying checklist
paper: Specialty coffee standards + contaminant-testing buyer framework
finding: Roast date, whole bean, origin, heavy-metal testing, mycotoxin testing, pesticide standards, decaf process, packaging, and price per cup beat every vague low-toxin claim on the shelf.
